details: Malicious package. During `pip install`, `setup.py` executed a payload that ran the host-profiling commands `lsb_release -a`, `uname -rs` and `uname -p`, queried `http://ip-api.com/line` for the public IP and ISP, and then connected to `api.telegram.org`, all observed in a sandboxed install. This is the exact runtime fingerprint of the WhiteSnake infostealer `setup.py` payload (the same family as `aeivasta` and `setnetwork`, whose recovered payload steals browser credentials and cookies, Telegram sessions and cryptocurrency wallets and uploads them to a Telegram bot). The `setup.py` (189 KB, sha256 ea213a1b9e658baba5a089b78644df4ecdc7f26af8d72271a3fdbaa48335213b) is padded to an unusual size, consistent with the embedded Windows executable in that family. It belongs to the WhiteSnake infostealer campaign on PyPI (April 2023); sibling packages such as libidrequest (MAL-2024-5318) and libideeee (MAL-2024-5315) are already recorded. The package has been removed from PyPI.
